title: Blowup refinement of an alteration
statement: Let $a:W\to Z$ be an alteration of integral reduced Noetherian schemes [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. There are a nowhere dense closed subscheme $R\hookrightarrow Z$, a blowup $\widetilde Z=\operatorname{Bl}_R(Z)\to Z$, a blowup modification $\widetilde W\to W$, and a finite surjective morphism $\widetilde W\to\widetilde Z$ over $Z$ [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], with the composite $\widetilde W\to W\to Z$ equal to $\widetilde W\to\widetilde Z\to Z$.

source.place: Lemma 2.5, p. 4 and Lemma 3.2.1 proof, p. 8 (author PDF lines 674--676).

proof.text: Because $a$ is an alteration, it is proper and is finite over a dense open of the integral scheme $Z$ [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. Properness gives finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Intersect that finite locus with the nonempty open supplied by generic flatness and local finite presentation [lem-sbc-generic-flat-finite-presentation], and choose a nonempty affine open $U$ in the intersection. The restriction $a_U:W\times_ZU\to U$ is finite, flat and locally of finite presentation, hence finite locally free by the definition [def-pc-finite-locally-free]. The affine $U$ is quasi-compact, and the Noetherian integral scheme $Z$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so the hypotheses of [lem-trf-finite-after-blowup] are met.

source.place: Tag 052A, Proposition 29.28.1 (generic flatness); companion Tag 051T, Lemma 10.118.3 in literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex; Tag 01W1 (proper morphisms).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-after-blowup] to obtain a $U$-admissible blow-up $v:\widetilde Z\to Z$ and a finite locally free strict transform $p:\widetilde W\to\widetilde Z$. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], the center ideal is the unit ideal on $U$ and $v^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. Thus $v$ is the blow-up of a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I$ with $\mathcal I|_U=\mathcal O_U$ [def-nagata-admissible-blowup]. Let $R=V(\mathcal I)\hookrightarrow Z$ with its closed-subscheme structure [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Since $R$ is disjoint from the dense open $U$, it is nowhere dense, and $\widetilde Z=\operatorname{Bl}_R(Z)$. The strict-transform-over-complement statement [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-over-complement] identifies $p$ over $v^{-1}(U)$ with the base change of $a_U$, so it is surjective there.

source.place: Tag 0B49, Lemma 29.27.1 (finite strict transform after an admissible blow-up); literature/stacks-project/divisors.tex, Tags 080D and 080E

proof.text: The map $p$ is finite because it is finite locally free [def-pc-finite-locally-free], hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] and universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its image is therefore closed and contains the open $v^{-1}(U)$. The latter is topologically dense in $\widetilde Z$ by [lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup], applied to the dense quasi-compact open $U\subseteq Z$ and the $U$-admissible blow-up $v$. Thus the closed image of $p$ is all of $\widetilde Z$, proving that $p$ is surjective and finite in the sense of [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

source.place: Tags 01W1 and 01W3 (proper maps are closed and finite maps are proper), with Tag 0B49

proof.text: Let $U_W=a^{-1}(U)\subseteq W$. Since $a$ is surjective, $U_W$ is a nonempty open in the integral scheme $W$, hence is dense; it is quasi-compact because $a_U$ is finite and $U$ is affine. Let $\widetilde W$ denote the strict transform used above and let $u:\widetilde W\to W$ be its projection. By [def-nagata-strict-transform] it is a closed subscheme of $W\times_Z\widetilde Z$, namely the scheme-theoretic closure of its open part over $Z\setminus R$, and $u$ and $p$ are the restrictions of the two projections. The projection $W\times_Z\widetilde Z\to W$ is proper: $v$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper], and properness is preserved by base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The closed immersion followed by this projection is proper [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. By [lemma-nagata-admissible-blowup-over-open], applied to $v$ and to the blow-up of $W$ in the extended ideal $\mathcal I\mathcal O_W$, the restriction of $u$ over $U_W$ is an isomorphism. The theorem [thm-nagata-strict-transform-is-blowup] identifies the strict transform with $\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I\mathcal O_W}(W)$; applying [lemma-nagata-conrad-dense-in-admissible-blowup] to the dense quasi-compact open $U_W\subseteq W$ and this admissible blow-up shows that $u^{-1}(U_W)$ is topologically dense in $\widetilde W$. Hence $u$ is a modification by [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data]. Finally the same blow-up identification gives the required blowup modification, and $a\circ u=v\circ p$ holds because both are the composite $\widetilde W\hookrightarrow W\times_Z\widetilde Z\to Z$ (the theorem also records this compatibility with the structure morphisms to $Z$).

Step 4: the strict transform is Bl_{IO_W}(W); this blowup is U_W-admissible with U_W=a^{-1}(U) nonempty and dense; it is an isomorphism over U_W and dense there, and proper, so u is a modification.
